items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: we’d have just the strings and this woman named Gayle Levant on the harp, doing the glissandos and all that stuff.

ctx.x: Oh brass and woodwinds. Well especially in Hollywood for the film scores, and when I was producing big pop records like Dionne Warwick and things like that. I’d cut the tracks wherever — Nashville, and back then it would be Atlanta or Nashville, or in L.A., but then you do your what they call your sweetening dates. And you’d go in and you’d have the big — well my string sections were usually 12 – 4 – 4 and 2. 12 violins, 4 violas, four celli, and 2 string basses. And if we had the budget I’d use like 18 violins…

string section. But then we’d have — if it was an orchestra date, not just a string date we would call it, we’d have just the strings and this woman named Gayle Levant on the harp, doing the glissandos and all that stuff. And then the brass section and the woodwind section. I think the biggest sections I worked with was 65 pieces. And you talk about — you don’t show stress but when you’ve got 65 people sitting out there on the clock, you better be starting on time, because you’ve got to get your three or four…
And you hope the fire alarm doesn’t go off like it did today.
